item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q004_ferritin_like_functional_divergence","answer":"SCOPe treats ferritins, ribonucleotide-reductase-like proteins, and manganese catalases as remote relatives within the all-alpha ferritin-like structural lineage, not as members of one interchangeable functional family. The relevant hierarchy is class a, All alpha proteins; fold a.25, Ferritin-like; superfamily a.25.1, Ferritin-like. Within that superfamily, ferritins are family a.25.1.1, ribonucleotide-reductase-like proteins are family a.25.1.2, and manganese catalases are family a.25.1.3. Thus the shared four-helix-bundle ferritin-like architecture and metal-binding core support homology at the superfamily/fold level, while the separate SCOPe families mark substantial divergence in sequence, active-site details, oligomerization, metal usage, and chemistry. Ferritin oxidizes and stores iron, R2-like ribonucleotide-reductase subunits generate a radical for nucleotide reduction, and manganese catalases disproportionate peroxide at a dimanganese center; those functions and metal specificities should not be transferred automatically across the three families. A structure from one family can be a remote fold template for another, but family-level annotation, catalytic residues, substrate chemistry, and cofactor identity need direct biochemical or family-specific sequence evidence rather than inference from the ferritin-like superfamily alone.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
